notes:
Company background: Tidewell builds a headless search product for mid-market DTC brands. They operate a multi-tenant index per merchant; want to replace heuristic reranker with a learned reranker that improves cart-adds and revenue per session. Typical catalog sizes 50k-2M SKUs depending on merchant.

POC goals: prove quality lift (NDCG@10 / MRR) on a representative eval set, validate online p95 latency for top-50 rerank, and estimate cost per 1k reranks for both hosted and dedicated setups. They will run both nightly offline scoring (for ranking features & re-compute ranks) and a low-latency online rerank for storefront queries.

Performance targets: online p95 <= 120ms for top-50 reranks (soft), sustain 100-150 QPS during peak marketing events, offline batch throughput target ~40k docs/min to finish nightly refresh windows. Cost constraint: prefer <$0.12 per 1k rerank calls across typical traffic patterns.

Model preferences: evaluating open quantized 13B-family models + a distilled 7B fallback. Interested in Redwood Optimize suggestions for quantization profiles and batching parameters. Also want per-prompt evals and regression alerts integrated into their CI pipeline.

Security and deployment: require SSO/SAML for console access, SOC2 evidence for compliance teams, audit logs for inference, and KMS integration. Some EU merchants require data residency; they asked about VPC/private deployment options for selected tenants.

Sales notes: mid-market buyer set: VP Product (Maya Sloan) + Head of Engineering (Omar Khalil) are primary decision-makers; Head of ML (Sofia Martins) running the evaluation. They are inclined to start on Hosted for speed, then move to Dedicated pilot if cost/latency and isolation look good.

Direct quotes: "We need nightly offline scoring to be operational without blowing up costs." — Head of ML (Sofia). "If dedicated gives stable p95 under 120ms and a fixed monthly spend, legal will sign the SOW." — VP Product (Maya).

Open items: finalize DPA language, confirm exact peak QPS numbers by merchant, define canary fallback behavior (dedicated -> hosted) during capacity spikes, clarify per-tenant data residency flow.

Suggested Redwood plays: provide a turnkey offline scoring template (S3->batch rerank->S3), a model routing plan (13B primary, 7B fallback) with cost estimates, and an engineering workshop to validate p95 at their sample traffic pattern.
